tools.color_intro: Pick a colour and see it the way a PRG32 program writes it: RGB24 (8 bits for each of red, green and blue) and RGB565, the format of the PRG32 screen, in hexadecimal, decimal and binary.
tools.hex_help: Type six hexadecimal digits, for example #FFCC00.
tools.table_caption: The same colour written in two formats and three number bases.
tools.how_rgb24: RGB24 keeps 8 bits for each colour: red is the top 8 bits, then green, then blue. 0xFF0000 is pure red, 0xFFFFFF white.
tools.how_rgb565: RGB565 fits a colour in 16 bits: the top 5 bits of red, the top 6 of green (eyes see green best) and the top 5 of blue. The lower bits are dropped, so nearby colours can look the same on the PRG32: compare the two swatches.
